title: Midweek Ops Sketchbook — January 20, 2027
content:
Purpose and context:
Quick handwritten-style update for the week — this doc is a cross-shift sketchpad intended for on-call handoff, triage notes, and short-term action items. Not a formal postmortem (those will follow where needed). Keep it light, highlight open questions and blockers.

Summary (top-line):
- Incidents: 2 minor-sev incidents since last handoff (cache eviction storm on Dedicate-A, transient auth errors in eu-west-1 gateway). No customer-facing SLA breaches as of 01/22.
- SLOs: Token-gen latency SLO at 99th percentile still trending near target but narrow margin on peak windows (95–98 ms target, 99th at ~102 ms during peak ingestion). Error budget remaining for token-gen: ~87%.
- On-call: Handoff notes below. Next rotation: Ravi -> Lina on 01/23 09:00 PT.

Incidents (short-form):
1) Cache eviction storm — Dedicated pool A (01/19 03:14–03:42 PT)
   - Symptoms: sudden spike in token latency for customers pinned to Dedicated-A; increased GPU mem allocations and repeated cold-starts for KV cache leading to extra ~30–70ms per request.
   - Mitigation timeline (fast notes):
     * 03:16: alert fired (latency + cache miss ratio) -> bridge created (Eleanor)
     * 03:20: rollback of recent autoscaler tweak (PR 998) to stabilize node churn (Tom)
     * 03:30: increased KV cache soft limits and temporarily disabled cross-tenant aggressive evictions (Ravi)
     * 03:42: metrics stabilised; latency returned to baseline
   - Root-cause hypothesis: autoscaler combined with a new cache reclamation heuristic caused premature eviction under a bursty sequence-length distribution.
   - Immediate action items:
     * Add circuit-breaker to autoscaler for cache-heavy pods (action: Tom, due 2027-01-28).
     * Add a synthetic load test to emulate bursty sequences during PR validation (action: Eleanor, due 2027-01-25).

2) Transient auth errors — eu-west-1 gateway (01/21 10:02–10:18 CET)
   - Symptoms: ~0.4% 5xx rate for token exchange; errors appeared during a deploy of a minor token-service change. Failover to secondary auth handled most traffic; small number of clients saw retries.
   - Mitigation: quick rollback of token-service sidecar (Lina), increased client-side retry window.
   - Follow-up: token-service integration test flaked under noisy network conditions — open ticket INF-412.

SLO snapshot and concerns:
- Token-gen latency SLO (P99) target: <= 110ms (global). Current observed: 99th = 106–112ms during peak; non-peak ~82–90ms.
- Embedding batch throughput SLO: 99% of batches processed < 250ms — currently holding at 98.6% on Dedicated clusters with quantized models.
- Error budget burn: small uptick this week driven by the eu-west auth flake; projected burn less than 5% this quarter if no regressions.
- Monitoring gaps to address: lack of sequence-length distribution metric surfaced during cache incident. Add sequence_length_histogram (action: Tom + Observability, due 2027-02-04).

Operational work / manual tweaks performed this week:
- Temporary autoscaler threshold adjustments in Dedicated-A (rolled back after incident).
- Patched retry/backoff TTL in client SDK for token exchange (Lina).
- Small Canary: rolled out a new kernel selection heuristic to 5% of traffic in us-central-1 — monitoring shows no regressions.

On-call handoff (what to watch for next 24–48h):
- Alerts to prioritize:
  * latency.p99.token-gen > 120ms sustained for 5m (P0)
  * cache.eviction.rate spike > 5x baseline (P1)
  * token-service.auth.5xx > 0.5% sustained (P1)
- Tactical runbook snippets: if cache.eviction spike -> temporarily increase cache soft limits, check autoscaler node churn, check recent PRs to autoscaler/cache reclaim.
- Who to call: Tom (autoscale/cache), Lina (token-service), Miguel (infra/GPU scheduling). Phone numbers in team directory.

Action items (tracked, short):
- Tom: implement autoscaler circuit-breaker and add unit tests to guard cache eviction heuristics. Due 2027-01-28.
- Eleanor: create synthetic sequence-length burst test and hook into CI (small cluster test). Due 2027-01-25.
- Lina: stabilize token-service integration tests, add flaky-test marker + retries. Due 2027-01-24.
- Observability (assigned to Ravi): add sequence_length_histogram and dashboard tile, add alert for unexpected distribution shifts. Due 2027-02-04.

Risks & unresolved questions:
- Is the autoscaler policy still the right default for Dedicated pools running mixed sequence lengths? We need a long-term plan: per-pool policy or per-model hints. (Discussion item for SRE+Serving runtime sync 01/27).
- Cost impact: temporarily increasing cache soft limits raised GPU memory pressure by ~7% during the incident window; need to quantify if that meaningfully increases unit cost for high-utilization customers. (Finance sync requested).

Meeting notes (standup highlights 01/20 and ad-hoc bridge 01/19):
- 01/19 bridge: agreed rollback of autoscaler tweak, added temporary guardrails, synthesized hypotheses for root cause.
- 01/20 weekly standup: briefed product on temporary customer impact (none durable), prioritized test infra and observability as top 3 follow-ups.

Quick wins to deploy this week:
- Add sequence-length sampling to telemetry (low-risk).
- Increase CI coverage for token-service under network noise (medium-risk).

Reference log snippets (for handoff use):
- Prometheus query to spot evictions: sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (pool)
- Quick latency query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))

Handoff checklist (for incoming):
- Confirm you can access the bridge channel and the runbook (links above).
- If you see cache spikes: pause new deploys to Dedicated-A and escalate to Tom.
- If token-service auth errors reappear: enable failover to auth-secondary (runbook step 4) and notify Lina immediately.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Draft postmortem content only after sequence_length metric available.
- Consider experiment: autoscaler cooldown window longer for pools with high cache state.

Appendix: recent PRs and diffs worth eyeballing:
- PR 998 (autoscaler scaling signal tweak) — ephemeral revert after incident.
- Kernel selection heuristic PR (rolling canary in us-central-1).

End of sketch — add items inline below as you triage through the day.

-- Eleanor K. (on-call, Jan 20–22 2027)
